explain_task.question: In the revised model, explain why the optimal LP relaxation picks `machine1_extended = 1`, `machine2_extended = 0`, `liquid_prod = 52.8`, and `solid_prod = 15.0`, even though the original model had only `x_liquid` and `x_solid`. Your answer must identify the exact CSV fields and parameter values that drive this result, connect them to the code constraints `prob += p['machine_1_time_per_liquid_lot']*xl + ... <= ... + p['extended_extra_minutes']*y1`, `prob += p['labor_hours_per_machine_extended']*(y1+y2) <= p['labor_budget_hours']`, and the objective terms involving `priority_liquid`, `priority_solid`, `excess_liquid`, `excess_solid`, and `extended_mode_penalty`. Also, using the solver output, name which constraints are binding or slack, report the relevant slack/dual values, and explain the business meaning of the positive dual on the binding machine-time constraint and why it cannot be linearly extrapolated to large changes in `extended_extra_minutes` or `priority_reserve_lots`.
